item.title: Irrationality of Square Root of 2
item.description:
1 Motivation

​ This is the first theorem that hooks me into mathematics. If you are studying real analysis using Stephen Abbot’s Understanding analysis {abbott2015understanding}, this is the first and foremost thing the author discusses. You might or might not be as impressed as I was when I first looked at this beauty of a proof, but mathematicians all admit that this is a beautiful proof due to its simplicity.

​ Although there are a handful of ways to proof it, I will provide one here that I find attractive.

TipChallenge: Can We Generalize This Result?

We have shown above that is irrational. But is this property unique to the number 2? We know so its rational. What about 3 or 5?

Challenge: Can we generalize this result to for any positive integer ? In other words, is the square root of every positive integer irrational?

If not, under what conditions is rational?

Hint: Consider the role of evenness in our proof. Can we replace it with a more general property of integers?
